text:
maria: Heads-up — observed a clear tail-latency spike (~250ms p99 -> 1.2s) on canary during a synthetic burst at 03:12 UTC. Looks tied to KV cache evictions under pressure.

sam: Saw that too. Repro with local load generator?

maria: Yes, ran a short repro on my dev rig with `--burst=500` and long context tokens. P95 is fine but p99 jumps when eviction starts.

aoife: Can you paste the log snippet?

maria: Sure — key lines: 
```
[03:12:09.124] evicter: pressure_entered hotset=0.82 free_pages=120
[03:12:09.135] pager: started page-out batch size=32 target_free=256
[03:12:09.137] evicter: fallback_path triggered -> fifo_fastpath=false
[03:12:09.138] runtime: kv-read blocked waiting for pager (owner_tid=42)
[03:12:09.370] runtime: kv-read resumed, latency=1236ms
```

sam: Interesting: `fallback_path triggered` log is from our new fallback which tries to compact fragmented slabs before full swap. If compaction stalls, readers block.

kevin: Where does correctness come into play? Is this just latency or are we losing entries?

maria: No loss observed, but we saw an ordering mismatch in one trace: a reinsert of a recently-evicted entry returned stale pointer for ~5ms until rebind. That looks like a race between eviction finalizer and reuse allocator.

aoife: Can you share the perf flame output?

maria: Pasted a short profile — top hotspots: 
- `evict_compact_slab` 38%
- `pager_batch_write` 22%
- `kv_lookup` blocked 18%
- `allocation_fastpath` 12%

perf-bot: CI test `kv-evict-stability` failed on canary (regression 0.9 -> 1.4s p99). See run: https://ci.internal/runs/2857

sam: Hypothesis: under bursty allocation, compacting tries to create contiguous free run but we hold per-slab locks too long. That blocks alloc and lookup threads; LRU vs FIFO choice influences fragmentation pattern.

maria: Agreed. In traces, FIFO kept moving older entries out, creating many small free holes; compaction had to run more often. LRU seems to cluster hot entries and reduces compaction frequency but has a heavier path for updating access timestamps.

kevin: Is this reproducible with LRU disabled?

maria: I ran a variant forcing FIFO-only and another forcing LRU-only in dev. FIFO-only -> frequent compaction + more fragmentation + p99 spikes. LRU-only -> less compaction but higher CPU per request, p99 stable under same burst.

aoife: We need a middle ground: heuristics to pick eviction policy based on observed hotset churn and available free_pages. Maybe: if hotset_retention > 0.6 and allocation_rate > X, prefer LRU; else FIFO.

sam: Another angle: make the fallback_path non-blocking. Instead of blocking readers during compaction, have compaction run incrementally with lock striping and use a short-circuit for readers to skip compacted regions.

maria: Incremental compaction sounds promising. I sketched an approach: compact in slices of 8 pages, yield after each slice, and publish a per-slab compacted-tip pointer. Readers check tip and can decide to proceed or briefly retry without global stall.

kevin: That reduces worst-case stall but might increase p50 due to occasional retries. Trade-off worth it if p99 improves.

aoife: Also add a diag counter and alert when fallback_path runtime > 100ms. We lacked observability here.

maria: I have reproduction steps and a minimal patch for incremental compaction. Opening a PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3912 (draft).

sam: Add a flag to switch policy selection at runtime so we can A/B test on canary.

maria: Will do. Also adding a small harness to simulate fragmentation patterns (alternating hot/cold keys) so CI can catch regressions early.

kevin: For correctness: add a sanity check in finalizer: before reusing a slot ensure the sequence number advanced and a CAS on the slot succeeds, otherwise delay reuse one tick. That should prevent the transient stale pointer case.

maria: Good call. I'll include CAS gate and a metric for CAS-retries.

perf-bot: Note: proposed changes will bump CPU by ~6% in LRU mode per bench run; ops okay with small increase for p99 gains?

kevin: Ops say we can accept CPU trade for stable p99 on canary with rollout guard.

aoife: Plan summary: (1) implement incremental compaction non-blocking fallback, (2) add runtime policy toggle + heuristic to pick LRU/FIFO, (3) CAS safety gate on reuse, (4) CI harness for fragmentation and alerts for fallback latency.

maria: I'll push the draft PR, add unit tests, and schedule a canary A/B run for tomorrow morning. Will tag @kevin @sam when ready.

sam: Awesome. If you need help with perf comparisons or flamegraph diffs ping me.

maria: Thanks — will do.

ci-bot: Automated note: created issue #712 - "kv: non-blocking compaction fallback and eviction policy heuristics" linking PR/3912.

maria: Closing loop: after patching in dev, p99 reduced from 1.2s -> 320ms under same synthetic burst. Not final but promising. Will share full graphs in PR. :tada:

kevin: Great progress. Keep the changes small and feature-flagged for rollback.

maria: Yep. Will also add a changelog entry under `kv-eviction` for the rollout notes.

sam: Thanks everyone.
